title: Territorial data changes in Geotrek need attribution that a Django model does not keep
content:
Makina Corpus works exclusively in free software — an SSLL in the French sense — on Python/Django, Symfony and PostgreSQL/GIS. One of its products, Geotrek, is used by French public bodies, which puts public data in a stack the firm controls from schema to interface.

The gap sits at the framework level. A Django model stores the current value of each field, so when a territorial dataset changes, the change itself is not retained as an attributed event. For data that public bodies publish and act on, the missing part is who changed what and when, and an ORM was never designed to keep it.

Two things make this lead unusually workable. The stack is one the firm builds in every day, so the record layer attaches at a familiar seam rather than arriving as an unfamiliar dependency, and the exclusive free-software commitment removes the licensing objection before it is raised. The gap itself is ordinary; the alignment is what makes it worth pursuing.
